system_description.narrative_title: AI-driven geopolitical scramble over chips, markets and security
system_description.narrative_summary: Rapid AI advances and high-profile model releases are sharply increasing demand for compute and memory, driving supply-chain stress, corporate strategy shifts, and a surge in investment. That tech-driven economic pressure is intersecting with US–China competition (trade, diplomacy, export controls) and rising cybersecurity and biosecurity concerns, producing policy pushback, industrial subsidies, and trade frictions. Feedbacks between model races, chip shortages, and geopolitical maneuvering are reshaping markets, national strategies, and risk governance in real time.
system_description.scope: Within this system: AI model development and deployment, demand for GPUs/memory and data‑center/cloud capacity; semiconductor and memory supply chains (fabs, tools, rare earths); major tech firms and AI infrastructure providers; national industrial policy, export controls, and diplomatic actions; financial markets and corporate strategy; and emerging security domains (cybersecurity, AI safety, biosecurity). Flows include compute, capital, talent, components, regulatory signals, and information/risk.
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economy and security order — technology-driven great‑power competition and the international trade/regulatory regime.
adjacent_subsystems: Semiconductor manufacturing & supply chains (fabs, tools, materials)
International trade and diplomacy (US–China–EU–Taiwan relations, export controls)
Global capital markets & corporate strategy (investors, consultancies, law firms)

variables.name: AI compute demand
variables.description: The aggregate demand for high‑performance compute (training and inference) required by AI models and services across the economy.

variables.name: Compute infrastructure capacity
variables.description: The installed capacity of data‑center and accelerator resources available for AI workloads, measured in usable accelerator-hours or equivalent.

variables.name: Semiconductor production rate
variables.description: The flow rate of manufactured semiconductors and memory components entering the supply chain per unit time.

variables.name: Fabrication lead time
variables.description: The average time between semiconductor order placement and delivery of finished chips or wafers to downstream users.

variables.name: Supply‑chain resilience
variables.description: The system's capacity to absorb, adapt to, and recover from disruptions in component, materials, and logistics flows.

variables.name: AI infrastructure investment rate
variables.description: The rate of new capital deployment into AI compute infrastructure, fabs, memory production, and related physical assets.

variables.name: AI talent stock
variables.description: The available pool of skilled personnel (researchers, engineers, designers) capable of designing, building, and operating advanced AI systems and chips.

variables.name: Export controls tightness
variables.description: The strictness and scope of trade and export restriction policies applied to advanced computing and semiconductor technologies.

variables.name: Industrial subsidy level
variables.description: The intensity of government financial support and incentives directed at semiconductor, memory, and AI infrastructure development.

variables.name: Compute market concentration
variables.description: The degree to which provision of AI compute capacity is concentrated among a small number of providers or platforms.

variables.name: Technology innovation rate
variables.description: The pace at which new AI architectures, accelerator designs, and semiconductor process technologies are developed and diffused.

variables.name: Cybersecurity risk level
variables.description: The prevalence and severity of cyber threats and vulnerabilities affecting AI systems, infrastructure, and data flows.

variables.name: Biosecurity risk level
variables.description: The assessed likelihood and potential impact of biological misuse or accidental harm facilitated by AI capabilities and tools.

variables.name: Regulatory scrutiny intensity
variables.description: The level of oversight, enforcement, and compliance pressure applied by regulatory bodies to AI development, deployment, and related markets.

variables.name: Information flow velocity
variables.description: The speed and openness with which technical knowledge, model outputs, benchmark results, and risk information circulate across actors and borders.

variables.name: Compute unit price
variables.description: The market price per unit of usable AI compute (e.g., per accelerator‑hour or equivalent), reflecting supply‑demand balance and cost structure.

catalysts.title: Surge in AI compute demand from new models
catalysts.description: Continued rollouts of large models and agent systems drive a sustained, rapid rise in demand for high‑performance compute for training and inference.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'AI computing demand may never be sated', 'OpenAI launches new Astra model', 'AI Infrastructure Will Cost Trillions More'.

catalysts.title: Ongoing memory‑chip squeeze ('RAMageddon')
catalysts.description: AI-driven demand and model launches keep memory and DRAM tight, sustaining price pressure and production bottlenecks in near term.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'RAMageddon hits consumer electronics', 'Why the launch of OpenAI’s latest Astra model reignited the memory chip trade', 'Memory chips have come to rule the AI boom.'

catalysts.title: Major chipmakers deploy ASML's newest tools
catalysts.description: Commitments by TSMC, Samsung and collaborations with ASML accelerate adoption of advanced lithography tools, affecting capacity and node progress.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'TSMC, Samsung commit to ASML’s newest chipmaking tools', 'ASML to work with major chipmakers...'

catalysts.title: Xi's US visit / Xi‑Trump summit
catalysts.description: High‑level summit and associated CEO delegation could alter chip diplomacy, export negotiations and trade tensions between US and China.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Ahead of Xi's US visit', 'EXCLUSIVE: China's Xi seeks to bring large CEO delegation on US visit', 'China lashes back at US... ahead of Xi‑Trump summit'.

catalysts.title: EU 'Buy European' procurement rules tabled
catalysts.description: EU plans to table public‑procurement rules favouring European suppliers, likely shifting procurement and industrial support away from China.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'EU to table ‘Buy European’ public procurement rules', 'EU wants initial Chinese action on trade gap by early October'.

catalysts.title: Taiwan expands chip diplomacy to allies
catalysts.description: Taiwan's targeted chip allocations and diplomatic offers to allies continue, reshaping supply access and geopolitical leverage over chips.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Taiwan flexes chip diplomacy muscles as it faces pressure to share AI wealth with allies'.

catalysts.title: China rare‑earth firms halt some US shipments
catalysts.description: Partial halts of rare‑earth shipments to the US create supply frictions that can reverberate through chip and materials supply chains.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'China rare earth firms halt some US shipments over geopolitical worries, sources say'.

catalysts.title: Regulatory scrutiny ramps on AI agents and bio‑risks
catalysts.description: Governments and multilateral bodies increase oversight and rules for agentic models and biological risk mitigation following high‑profile launches and warnings.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'OpenAI launches new Astra model amid growing scrutiny', 'AI could pose ‘existential’ risk', 'AI groups race to limit bioweapon risks'.

catalysts.title: Enterprise AI security and CISO elevation
catalysts.description: High‑profile attacks and AI‑specific vulnerabilities spur a wave of security hiring and spending, elevating CISOs and reshaping vendor demand.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Meet the CISO: A new front line star in the AI cybersecurity war', 'Hugging Face attack is a wake‑up call', 'AI spots cyber gaps faster than financial firms can fix them'.
